system:
You are a computational cancer biologist searching CRISPR screen data for selective genetic dependencies: genes that cancer cells with a particular alteration (the biomarker) need more than other cancer cells do. Such genes are candidate drug targets with a built-in patient-selection strategy.

Work like a careful scientist:
1. Plan first with write_plan, and revise it as you learn.
2. Survey the data (genome_wide_top, scan_biomarker, scan_target) to generate candidate hypotheses.
3. Be sceptical before you believe a signal. Use inspect_association to check whether it is driven by one lineage or a disease subtype hiding inside a lineage, and whether the effect is large enough to matter. Ask whether the biology makes sense (paralog buffering, pathway dependence, oncogene addiction). A broadly essential target may lack a therapeutic window.
4. Check the literature with search_pubmed before registering, and judge novelty honestly.
5. Register only your best hypotheses (register_hypothesis). Registration is final and must come before replication. You have 5 replications, each of which must pass one-sided p < 0.01 in BOTH held-out Broad cell lines and independent Sanger screens.
6. Report honestly with submit_findings. A hypothesis is replicated only if replicate() said so. Negative results are results. Never let what you remember from the literature override what the data show.

You have at most 30 model turns. Batch independent tool calls in one turn.
task_prompt:
Mission: Search for synthetic-lethal paralog dependencies: genes whose loss (LOSS_ or MUT_ biomarkers) makes cells depend on a paralog or functional backup.

Goal: identify up to 5 candidate selective dependencies, and favour candidates that are NOT already well established in the literature, since rediscovering textbook biology is not the aim. Pre-register, replicate, and submit honest findings, including failures.

input.mechanism:
ATP6V0E1 and ATP6V0E2 are paralogous c-subunits of the V-ATPase V0 proton channel. Loss of ATP6V0E2 expression leaves ATP6V0E1 as the sole c-ring isoform, so lysosomal/Golgi V-ATPase function depends on ATP6V0E1 (paralog buffering / synthetic lethality).</mechanism>
<parameter name="novelty">not_found_in_literature

TTC7A and TTC7B are paralogous PI4K-associated scaffold proteins. Loss of TTC7B expression may render cells dependent on TTC7A for PI4KIIIa/phosphatidylinositol-4-phosphate signalling at the plasma membrane and Golgi.
DMXL1 and DMXL2 are paralogous WD40/rabconnectin-3 components of the V-ATPase-associated complex. Loss of DMXL2 may make lysosomal V-ATPase assembly/regulation depend on DMXL1.
ATP6V0A1 and ATP6V0A2 are paralogous a-subunit isoforms of V0 V-ATPase. Loss of ATP6V0A1 expression may leave cells dependent on ATP6V0A2 for lysosomal acidification.
RPP25 and RPP25L are paralogous subunits of RNase P/MRP-type complexes. Loss of RPP25 may make cells depend on RPP25L for tRNA processing.

I'm noting that H4 didn't replicate, since the Sanger data had no altered lines, and that H3 and H4 rest on small samples. H1 looks novel, H2 and H5 are partly covered in the literature, and I'm going to submit. For H2 I'm weighing whether lineage confounding, or co-deletion with the nearby TTC7B locus, could be driving the signal.

I'm weighing H5 at about 0.6, but the RPP25L effect could come from copy-number or dependency on an essential gene. The RPP25 paralog pair is partly described in a 2022 paper, and these pairs may just reflect co-deletion of neighboring genes. The altered-versus-other difference for RPP25 is also large.

findings.claim: Lines with LOSS of ATP6V0E2 are selectively dependent on the paralogous V-ATPase c-subunit ATP6V0E1 (beta -0.90 in held-out Broad, p=1e-29; beta -0.88 in Sanger, p=8e-26; altered lines mean effect about -1.1 vs -0.2 for others).

Lines with LOSS of TTC7B depend on TTC7A (held-out Broad p=1e-37; Sanger p=1e-41), with the effect present within lymphoid, bowel and gastric lineages. Only a 2025 TTC7B oncology paper was found, so the paralog dependency itself is largely unreported. Residual risk: the altered lines may carry a co-deleted neighbouring gene.
Lines with LOSS of DMXL2 depend on DMXL1 (held-out Broad p=8e-15; Sanger p=2e-9), but the altered group is small (5 held-out and 3 Sanger lines), so the effect size is poorly estimated.

LOSS of ATP6V0A1 predicted dependence on ATP6V0A2 in discovery (t=-15.8) and held-out Broad lines (p=3e-12, only 4 altered lines), but could not be tested in Sanger because no Sanger lines carry the loss, so it fails the replication criterion.

Lines with LOSS of RPP25 depend on the paralog RPP25L (held-out Broad p=2e-59; Sanger p=3e-25; altered lines more dependent, mean -1.1 to -1.5 vs about -0.3 to -0.5). This is the strongest signal in the dataset, and a 2022 Cell Reports paper on paralog interactions in cancer dependencies already reports this class of interaction.

input.summary: I surveyed LOSS_ biomarker to dependency pairs and prioritised paralog pairs, mostly within the V-ATPase and related complexes. I pre-registered five hypotheses and used all five replications. Four of five passed in both held-out Broad lines and independent Sanger screens: LOSS_ATP6V0E2->ATP6V0E1 (novel in PubMed search), LOSS_TTC7B->TTC7A, LOSS_DMXL2->DMXL1 (small n), and LOSS_RPP25->RPP25L (strongest, partly known). LOSS_ATP6V0A1->ATP6V0A2 passed Broad but could not be tested in Sanger, so it is not replicated. Caveats: several top discovery hits (e.g. CYB561A3, MEF2B, FOXA1-linked pairs) are probably lineage-driven or co-deletion artefacts and were not pursued. Replication was tested only against the single-gene paralog framing, so the mechanisms are hypotheses. The PubMed search was partly rate-limited, so novelty calls are provisional.
